facts.text: The George Nakashima Woodworker Complex in Solebury is a National Historic Landmark, honoring a pioneer of modern furniture design.
Solebury Township boasts four National Historic Landmarks and six National Historic Districts, with over 400 homes dating back to the 18th and 19th centuries.
Before European settlement, the area now known as Solebury was inhabited by the Lenape Turtle Tribe, one of three Algonquian groups in the Delaware River valley.
In 1702, English Quakers carved out Solebury Township from Buckingham lands, and by 1703 it already had 24 landowners and 28 farm tracts.
Mills powered by local streams produced wood, grain, paper, silk, and limestone products, making Solebury a bustling industrial hub in the 18th and 19th centuries.
During the early 1990s, the rock duo Ween recorded their albums *The Pod* and *Pure Guava* in an apartment on Van Sant Road in Solebury.
